I came in because I absolutely cannot stop focusing on my face. Specifically, the left side of my face. It's just so incredibly uneven and puffy, and it's driving me crazy.

And it's not just at work, either. It completely ruins the memory of the night because all I can see is this glaring puffiness. The frustrating thing is, I'll point it out to my friends, I'll literally show them the photo on my phone and zoom in on the exact spot, and everyone keeps telling me they don't see anything. My sister even got mad at me the other day because I kept asking her to look at my cheek. They all say I look fine, but I know what I'm seeing. 

And it's just... it's really starting to mess with my work and my social life. I keep turning my camera off during important meetings and my manager has started making comments about it, and my social life is basically non-existent right now because I don't want anyone taking pictures of me at the dance socials. Yeah, it's... it's just bleeding into everything, honestly, and it's so incredibly frustrating because I feel like I'm watching my life just sort of shrink. 

With my job, for instance, we have these strict service level agreements, like deadlines for closing out support tickets, and I've actually missed some of those ticket deadlines recently. Which is so completely unlike me because I've always prided myself on being really efficient. But I'll get so caught up in the bathroom mirror, or I'll be obsessively checking my webcam preview before I have to talk to a user, trying to adjust my hair or the lighting to find an angle where my left cheek doesn't look so huge and swollen, and I just completely lose track of time. I've even joined several video calls late because I just couldn't get past how I looked in the preview window. I'd sit there with my mouse hovering over the 'join' button, just feeling totally paralyzed and sick about it. And it got to the point where my supervisor actually brought it up during my last performance review. He sat me down and said my metrics were slipping and noted that I'd been late logging into client meetings, and it was just... it was mortifying. I couldn't exactly tell him, you know, 'Oh, it's because I'm staring at my puffy face,' so I just had to sit there and take the hit to my professional reputation.

And then socially, it's exactly the same thing. I've basically isolated myself. Like I mentioned the salsa dancing earlier? I've been skipping so many salsa nights lately. And it's not just that, it's other community events, too, like local street fairs or group meetups that I usually love going to. Because I just know—I absolutely know—someone is going to have a camera or their phone out. People love taking photos at these things and putting them right on social media, and if I know there's even a chance people will be taking photos, I just can't bring myself to go anymore. I'll actually get all dressed up, do my makeup, and then I'll look in the mirror before I leave and see how lopsided my face is, and I just... I take my shoes off and stay home. It's just easier than dealing with the sheer panic of waiting for the photos to be posted so I can scrutinize them or try to untag myself, but it's just... I don't know, it's making me really lonely, but I just can't stop worrying about it.

I mean... I've definitely thought about it. Of course I've thought about it. I've spent, I don't even know how many hours, just sitting at my computer late at night, long after I should be asleep, just typing things into Google like 'unilateral facial swelling' or 'left cheek puffiness treatments.' And I'll end up on these websites for plastic surgeons or fancy dermatology clinics, looking at all their procedures and before-and-after photos, trying to see if anyone else has a face that looks like mine and what they did to fix it. 

But... no, I haven't actually made an appointment or gone to see anyone like that. And I think... honestly, I think it's because I'm just so completely terrified of what they'll say. Like, what if I take time off work, which I'm already struggling with, and I pay for an expensive consultation, and I sit in their pristine little waiting room, and then I go in and point out the puffiness... and they just do exactly what my sister and my coworkers do? What if they just look at me like I'm crazy and tell me they don't see anything? 

I don't think I could handle that. It's bad enough when my friends brush it off and tell me I'm fine, but if a professional—like a plastic surgeon whose entire job is to look at facial structure and symmetry—if they were to dismiss me and tell me I'm making it up when I can clearly see this massive swelling in the mirror... I just wouldn't know what to do. It would be absolutely devastating. So I just... I haven't gone. I just keep endlessly researching, and staring at my webcam preview, and trying to figure out if there's some kind of extreme makeup contouring trick I can use to hide it instead. Actually going to a surgeon just feels like this huge, terrifying hurdle, because I just... I really need someone to acknowledge that it's real first, you know? I couldn't bear being told I'm imagining it by someone who's supposed to help me.

I... I mean, I hear what you're asking. And I guess, logically, on some level... I know that's what people are telling me. I mean... I feel like we are kind of going in circles here, but I really want to try to answer you. Are you asking if I think I'm just... imagining it entirely? Like it's literally zero percent real and one hundred percent just in my head?
